source: Wisconsin Administrative Code NR 27.03 (Endangered and threatened species), Register November 2024 No. 827
note: Plants that NR 27 lists only as a variety or subspecies are left out, because the plant AI can't tell varieties apart. Only plants that the DNR's Natural Heritage Inventory lists for our county are kept.

plants.lookFor: A small orchid with a white, pouch-shaped flower, often with thin purple lines, and twisted greenish side petals. It blooms in late May and early June.
plants.why: It only grows in wet prairies and fens, and very few of those are left.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: Jason Sturner, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons

plants.lookFor: A spike of pale purple to white star-shaped flowers (6 petals each) on a stem 1 to 2 feet tall, with long, grass-like leaves at the bottom. It blooms from late April to May.
plants.why: It grows in only a few leftover wet prairies, often along roads and railroads.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: Thomas G. Barnes, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain, Wikimedia Commons

plants.lookFor: A milkweed up to 6 feet tall with a round cluster of bright pink to purple flowers at the top, and leaves in pairs that are hairy underneath. Common milkweed's flowers are much paler. It blooms in June and July.
plants.why: Very few are left in Wisconsin, in open oak woods and along the edges of woods.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: Katja Schulz, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons

plants.lookFor: An orchid with a tall spike of creamy white flowers. Each flower has a lip with a frilly fringe. It blooms in July in wet prairies.
plants.why: It needs wet prairies, and very few are left. It's threatened in the whole country, too.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: Mike Redmer, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain, Wikimedia Commons

plants.lookFor: A hairy plant 1 to 2 feet tall with pale purple, trumpet-shaped flowers right next to the leaves. Its leaves grow in pairs and have hairy edges. It blooms from late May to October.
plants.why: It grows in only a few prairies and oak woods in Wisconsin.

plants.lookFor: A hairy stem 8 to 16 inches tall with a fuzzy spike of small yellow flowers, and big egg-shaped, toothed leaves at the bottom. It looks like a small common mullein. It blooms in late May and June.
plants.why: It's rare all over the world. In Wisconsin it grows in small openings in woods and near the edges of bluffs.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: Erica Tava Johnson, CC BY 4.0, iNaturalist

plants.lookFor: A prairie plant with leaves in threes made of narrow, silvery leaflets, and thin spikes of small, pale yellowish flowers in August.
plants.why: It grows on only a few gravelly and sandy hillside prairies. It's threatened in the whole country, too.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: aarongunnar, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons

plants.lookFor: A short thistle (1 to 2 feet tall) with one or a few big pink-purple flower heads. It is less prickly than weedy thistles. It blooms in July and August.
plants.why: It lives in dry prairies that are disappearing, and people sometimes pull it by mistake because they think it is a weedy thistle.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: Julie McLaughlin, CC BY 4.0, iNaturalist

plants.lookFor: Pale pink petals that droop straight down from a big, spiky brown center, on a tall stem with long, narrow, hairy leaves. It blooms in June and July.
plants.why: It only grows in prairies, and most prairies have been turned into farms and towns.
plants.photoCredit: Photo: Erica Tava Johnson, CC BY 4.0, iNaturalist

plants.lookFor: A low milkweed, under 1 foot tall, with fuzzy stems and leaves and one round ball of small greenish-yellow flowers at the top. It blooms in early summer.
plants.why: It only grows in dry, sandy or gravelly prairies, and very few of those places are left.
